data.spiritual_significance: Arjir holds immense spiritual significance as it is derived from the name of Arjuna, a devoted and revered disciple of Lord Krishna. In Hindu spirituality, Arjir represents the ideals of selfless devotion, wisdom, and courage on the spiritual journey. It embodies the concepts of balanced action and holy war, as Arjuna did when he fought the Kurukshetra battle. Ultimately, Arjir signifies spiritual growth encompassing inner strength, wisdom, and strong character, striving to serve a higher purpose in life.

historical_references.context: Arjir is one of the five Pandava brothers, sons of King Pandu and Queen Kunti. Along with his brothers, he undergoes a twelve-year exile in the forest and later engages in a battle for the throne of Hastinapura against their cousins, the Kauravas. Arjir is considered one of the greatest archers in Hindu mythology and is revered for his skills in warfare.
